newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures recover on U.S. grind data.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures recover on U.S. grind data.

text.p: London cocoa futures nudged up slightly in early afternoon on Friday, encouraged by New York's advance on what some say was a bullish U.S. second quarter cocoa grind data.
By 1402 GMT, second-month September contract was traded three stg up at 1,027 stg a tonne after hovering in the minus terrritory all morning.
U.S. cocoa grindings rose 17.54 percent compared with the same year-ago period, to 97,223 tonnes, according to data released just before the New York opening on Friday.
"It's at the higher end of most people's expectations," said one London broker. "It's quite a friendly figure."
Most industry analysts had expected the data to show a rise of between five and 10 percent.

The U.S. numbers followed a mixed second quarter trend in Europe. Data released earlier this month showed Dutch grind rising more than 10 percent while German and UK grinds fell 3.5 and 4.1 percent respectively over the same quarter 1996.
Commenting on the U.S. figures, broker GNI Ltd said they implied an upward revision in consumption of only around 10,000 tonnes.
"One quarter's grind by itself doesn't mean a lot," said Lawrence Eagles, head of research at GNI. "It shows stock building's going on. It's a reasonable figure."
He said he was looking for a rise of perhaps 13 per cent in the third quarter. "People who get hyper-excited about this are probably overdoing it." -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
